title: MCP Protocol: Why Stdio Over HTTP Server
summary: KM exposes all functionality through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) over stdio, not a web server. LLM agents connect directly to the MCP server as a subprocess.

content.overview: Knowledge Manager uses MCP (Model Context Protocol) as its sole integration protocol. There is no REST API, no GraphQL, no gRPC. The MCP server runs as a stdio subprocess started by the LLM agent host (Claude Code, VS Code Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf). This keeps the architecture radically simple — no network ports, no authentication middleware, no CORS, no rate limiting.
content.details:
MCP is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol transmitted over stdin/stdout. The agent host spawns `km serve` as a child process and communicates via newline-delimited JSON messages. KM registers resources (for read-only data like index, health, stats) and tools (for actions like search, load, graph analysis).

The MCP server is built with FastMCP, a Python framework that handles the protocol plumbing. KM's create_server() function (mcp_server.py) assembles the server with all resources and tools registered as decorators.

Resources: knowledge://index, knowledge://health, knowledge://health/{key}, knowledge://stats, knowledge://recommendations, knowledge://changelog, knowledge://changelog/{key}, knowledge://federation/index.

Tools: load_module, search_modules, list_categories, expand_module, deep_search, knowledge_graph, federated_search.

In federation mode, additional namespaced resources are registered: knowledge://{ns}/index, knowledge://{ns}/health, knowledge://{ns}/stats, knowledge://{ns}/changelog.
content.references: See mcp_server.py:create_server() for the full server assembly. See connect.py for the platform connector that generates MCP config files. The MCP protocol spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io
content.caveats: Stdio transport means one MCP server per agent session. If the agent host disconnects, the server exits. This is by design — KM is stateless between sessions (all state is in the JSON files). For SSE or streamable HTTP transport (Phase 4+), FastMCP supports it but KM has not yet implemented it. The {module_key} resource template cannot handle values containing '/' due to FastMCP URI template limitations — module keys with slashes must use workarounds.
